direction: D2: Case/experience memory instead of (or beside) rules: retrieve 2-3 similar past training cases ("task feature -> failure -> fix") into the solver prompt at solve time (ExpeL / AWM / Dynamic Cheatsheet / ACE / Reflexion lineage).
title: Case memory on SearchQA is null-to-negative against the task-card Skill (5 up / 7 down of 100), and its only robust gain is an answer leak; not a replacement for rules
verdict_cn:
结论：不建议用"案例记忆"代替规则，可行性低。
做法：从 SearchQA（检索问答）第一阶段的 30 道训练错题，让 GLM 模型各写一条"案例"（题目特点、错在哪、该怎么做）。解题时按字面相似度挑最像的 2 条附在任务说明书后，让 deepseek 模型在另外 100 道训练题上各做 2 遍，与只用说明书的版本逐题对比。
结果：5 题变好、7 题变差、88 题不变，平均低 1 分（百分制，95% 可信范围 -6 到 +4），等于没效果；同一说明书重跑一遍本身就有 10 题变动。唯一两遍都变好的题，是案例里恰好写着另一道题相同的标准答案，属于泄题。变差的原因：一条"只写姓"的案例被套到 23 道题上，把"Ronald Reagan"写成"Reagan"，另一条案例却教"写全名加爵位"，这个数据集答案写法本身前后不一。即使按每题真实错因挑案例（解题时做不到），也只多对约 2 题。
文献：大收益集中在 ALFWorld（文字版家务机器人任务）、网页操作这类环境反复出现的任务；短答案问答只有约 +3 分，且比的是没有好说明书的弱基线；跨数据集迁移靠总结出的规则，不靠案例。
建议：主线继续做规则，借鉴三点：规则带适用条件、按后续效果记好坏账并删坏规则、示例写成抽象形式并对全题库答案查泄题。本次花 191 万 token（模型计费单位，上限 200 万）。

Pilot re-analysis (no new paid calls): under both truncation policies, against the same-text noise reference, by v3 pattern, item-by-item for the discordant items, an answer-leak audit, power/sample sizes, and the oracle arm recomputed against the complete parent cells (the draft's n=10 version had used partial cells).
Literature: verified 13 papers against their arXiv/ACL pages (Reflexion, ExpeL, AutoGuide, LEAP, RICP, AWM, Learn-by-Interact, Dynamic Cheatsheet, Memento, ReasoningBank, ACE, Xiong et al. ACL 2026, KATE). Corrected 3 numbers or quotes, dropped unverifiable claims and venues.
Wrote the final report (supersedes the draft) to the Mac scratchpad and the new machine. Spent no further paid tokens (pilot total 1,913,778 of 2,000,000).
evidence:
MEASURED (pilot: 100 I-ds check-half SearchQA TRAINING items x 2 runs; parent = I-ds step-0 Skill, digest ee9b737f = the v3 cells' skill_sha256; cases arm = parent + top-2 BM25 cases from 30 GLM-written cases built from the 30 proposal-half items that failed in either chain; 0 overlap between case sources and evaluated items):
- cases vs fresh parent (truncation = fail, as v3): 5 up / 7 down / 88 ties, mean -0.010, 95% bootstrap CI [-0.060, +0.040], sign p = 0.77. Accuracy parent 149/200, cases 147/200.
- Truncated runs excluded (99 items): 4/7/88, -0.015 [-0.061, +0.035].
- Noise reference, same parent text re-run vs v3 cells: 3 up / 7 down / 90 ties, -0.030 [-0.070, +0.005].
- By v3 pattern: both-pass items 2 up / 5 down (n=73); mixed 2/1 (n=9); both-fail 1/1 (n=18). The case block changed the final answer in 22 of 200 runs (15 items).
- Leak: 3 of 100 evaluated items had their reference inside a retrieved case. The only item fixed in both runs, "(Sir Francis) Drake", got it from case c28's own anchor reference "Sir Francis Drake" (one of 21 normalised answers shared by two SearchQA pool items). Without the 3 items: 4 up / 7 down, -0.021 [-0.067, +0.026].
- Mechanism: hub case c20 ("respond with just the surname") was retrieved for 23 of 100 items and produced "Reagan", "Alley", "Bush". The bank also holds the opposite lessons c28/c03 ("include the honorific").
- Oracle bound (cases chosen by the item's OWN v3 code, not observable at solve time), 27 v3-failed items: 3 up / 1 down / 23 ties, +0.074 [-0.019, +0.204], p = 0.63. That is about +2.0 points on the 100-item panel if no harm elsewhere (estimated).
- Item-difference SD 0.245, so 80% power (one-sided 5%) needs ~149 items for +5 points, ~412 for +3, ~926 for +2.
- Cost: prompt +349 tokens per cell (+9.3%); rendered Skill 14,116-14,419 bytes (cap 20,000).
MEASURED (v3 data):
- I-ds SearchQA stage 1: 90 failed runs, 42 of them (47%) the right entity in the wrong form, in both directions ("Arthur", "Fragonard" vs "Sir Francis Drake", "Sir Isaac Newton").
- Dominant I-ds codes: OfficeQA D2 41 / D1 30 / D3 20 of 111; LiveMath D1 85 of 134; SpreadsheetBench D4 25 of 43; ALFWorld D3 search loop 45 of 56.
- Pools are singleton families (SearchQA 600/600; LiveMath 100/100). OfficeQA: 74 items cite 114 bulletin issues; 29 of 74 share an issue with another item.
- ALFWorld I-ds episode: mean 105,651 tokens over 31.3 model calls.
CLAIMS (papers, verified this session):
- ExpeL: HotpotQA 28.0 -> 39.0 (retrieval-only 31, insights-only 36); ALFWorld 40 -> 59; HotpotQA -> FEVER transfer 63 -> 70 by insights only.
- AutoGuide: ALFWorld 54.5 -> 79.1.
- QA-side gains: LEAP HotpotQA +3.3; RICP CSQA/StrategyQA -0.2 to +4.3; Memento SimpleQA F1 +3.7.
- Losses without labels: Dynamic Cheatsheet GPT-4o MMLU-Pro Eng 53.2 -> 44.0, GPT-4o-mini AIME 16.7 -> 13.3; ACE finance, DC online without labels 65.4 vs base 69.1.
- More retrieved items can hurt: ReasoningBank best at k=1 (49.7 -> 44.4 at k=4).
- Xiong et al. (ACL 2026): experience-following; add-all memory banks stay flat or decline.
design:
Case = one diagnosed TRAINING failure item from the proposal half (the v4 per-item diagnosis), written by GLM:
- an observable applies_when predicate (<= 220 chars), mistake (<= 160), lesson (<= 260)
- an ABSTRACT anchor, never the literal reference (the pilot's concrete anchors leaked)
- mechanically leak-checked against EVERY pool answer, not only its own (21 shared normalised answers in the SearchQA pool)
- validated JSON and lengths; re-ask with the validation error
Retrieval: lexical BM25 is rejected by the pilot (it matches topic, not failure type). Use the D4 applicability judge over the case predicates (one GLM call per task, ~4k tokens), top-1/2, with abstention when nothing applies (AutoGuide). A failure-code classifier is bounded by the oracle arm (+2 points), and cannot work for the form codes D1/D2, which are defined relative to the reference.
Injection: a fixed-header block at the end of the bench's section, reserved budget <= 2 cases x 800 chars = 1.6 KB. Measured on I-ds: 14.1-14.4 KB rendered (cap 20 KB), +349 prompt tokens per cell. Identity becomes a POLICY hash (bank + retriever + header + k) plus the rendered-text hash and case ids per cell; test-evaluation reuse must key on the policy hash.
Gate without a validation set:
- one package decision per step on a fresh batch of training items not used for case writing (D1)
- arms: parent / parent + retrieved memory / parent + shuffled memory (the control for retrieval relevance)
- accept if the one-sided lower 95% bounds of (memory - parent) and (memory - shuffled) are both > 0, plus the C2/C3 analogues on regression panels with D8's margins
- sizes from the measured SD 0.245: +5 points needs ~150 items x 2 runs, +3 needs ~410
- after acceptance only: per-case helpful/harmful tallies from retrieval logs, and history-based deletion of net-negative cases (ACE, Xiong et al.)
Cross-bench: the bank is local by construction, so it contributes nothing to dissimilar benches and reaches similar benches only through abstraction into a rule (the rule pathway).
Per bench:
- SearchQA: measured null.
- OfficeQA: could key on the cited bulletin issue (29 of 74 items share one); untested, underpowered at 74 items.
- LiveMath: the meta-option lesson clashes with the option-text leak rule (D7).
- SpreadsheetBench: D3/D14.
- ALFWorld: the AutoGuide state->guideline form, the only bench with strong literature support.

pilot.result: Primary (truncation = fail, as v3), 100 SearchQA training items x 2 runs: cases vs task-card parent 5 up / 7 down / 88 ties, mean -0.010, 95% CI [-0.060, +0.040], p = 0.77 (parent 149/200, cases 147/200). Same-text noise reference 3 up / 7 down. With truncated runs excluded: 4/7/88, -0.015 [-0.061, +0.035]. Harm sits on items the parent already solved (both-pass: 2 up / 5 down of 73), driven by contradictory answer-form lessons (the 'surname only' case was retrieved for 23 items). The only item fixed in both runs is an answer leak through a shared pool answer. Oracle bound (the item's own v3 code), 27 failed items: 3 up / 1 down, +0.074 [-0.019, +0.204], i.e. about +2 points on the panel (estimated). Tokens: main 1,619,278 + oracle 226,144 + GLM case writing 68,356 = 1,913,778. Deviation: max_tokens 8,192 instead of 32,768 (2 truncated parent cells, both runs of one item); the verdict is the same under either truncation policy.

risks:
1. Answer leakage through concrete anchors and shared pool answers (measured 3 of 100 evaluated items; the only robust gain was a leak). Needs abstract anchors and a leak check against all pool answers.
2. Experience-following over-application: lessons fire where they do not fit despite the 'use only if the same situation applies' header. 22 of 200 runs changed answers; net harm on passing items (2 up / 5 down of 73).
3. SearchQA's reference conventions are inconsistent (surname-only vs full name with honorific), so form lessons contradict each other. No memory can fix annotation inconsistency (47% of I-ds failures are form errors).
4. Protocol identity: task-dependent prompts break the one-text-per-arm identity and test-evaluation reuse; a policy hash and per-cell case ids are required.
5. Power: a single-step package gate on SearchQA-sized batches detects only effects of about +5 points or more. The plausible effect (pilot plus literature) is 0 to +3.
6. Cost: an applicability judge per task (~4k GLM tokens); on ALFWorld every one of ~31 calls per episode carries the memory.
7. Strategic misfit: a case bank is bench-local by construction, so it cannot deliver the owner's cross-benchmark generalisation metric, and it does not exercise the generated-task (co-evolution) pathway.
8. Pilot limits: one bench, one chain's halves, 30 cases, lexical retrieval, 2 runs, no shuffled or placebo memory arm, max_tokens 8,192, oracle arm run only on the failed items. None of these can turn 5 up / 7 down into a detectable gain, since even the oracle bound is about +2 points.
cost_estimate:
MEASURED unit costs: 2.28k GLM tokens per case (68,356 for 30); 4,048 solver tokens per SearchQA pilot cell; +349 prompt tokens per cell with 2 cases (+9.3%); 105,651 tokens per I-ds ALFWorld episode (31.3 calls).
ESTIMATED:
- Banks for all five benches per chain: ~1-1.5M GLM tokens (I-ds failed items per stage: 54 / 59 / 75 / 43 / 32; OfficeQA and ALFWorld contexts are longer).
- Applicability judge: ~0.8M GLM tokens per 200-item batch.
- SearchQA package gate, 150 items x 2 runs x 3 arms: ~3.7M solver tokens per step.
- Headroom diagnostic (case writer + oracle-code probe) on SearchQA: ~0.3M tokens.
- Optional ALFWorld within-bench memory study (57 items x 2 runs x 3 arms = 342 episodes): ~36M tokens with short state-conditioned guidelines, up to ~70M with full trajectory demonstrations re-sent at every call.
- Test-time overhead: ~+9% on SearchQA cells.
Spent in this direction: 1,913,778 tokens (within the 2M cap); no further paid calls.
recommendation:
1. Do NOT replace rules with case memory in v5 for SearchQA, OfficeQA or LiveMath. The reasons are measured: a null-to-negative pilot, an oracle bound of about +2 points, form-dominated and directionally inconsistent failures, singleton-family pools, and no cross-benchmark transfer.
2. Import three memory mechanisms into the rule pathway (cheap, consistent with v4's conditional template and D4):
   (a) every rule carries an observable applicability predicate, and the solver abstains when it does not hold (AutoGuide);
   (b) accepted rules keep helpful/harmful paired tallies from later steps' training runs, with history-based deletion (ACE, Xiong et al.);
   (c) examples inside rules are abstract, and rules are leak-checked against every pool answer, not only their own items' (the pilot's realised leak).
3. Keep the case writer and the oracle-code probe as a cheap headroom diagnostic (~0.3M tokens per bench on SearchQA; cross-reference D9).
4. If the paper needs a memory baseline, run it ONLY on ALFWorld, as within-benchmark evidence (cross-reference D14): 45 of 56 I-ds failures are search loops, and ExpeL/AutoGuide report +19 to +25 points there. Arms parent / memory / shuffled memory, ~36M tokens with short guidelines. Never present it as generalisation.
5. OfficeQA same-document retrieval (29 of 74 items share a bulletin issue) is an untested, underpowered hypothesis; do not prioritise it.
